- When sentiment turns bullish (↑) after a downtrend, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After strong bullish sentiment spikes, model often overcorrects downward — adjust downward bias by 3–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish, model consistently overestimates — apply 2–4% downward bias.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak or negative — add 2–5% upward bias if sentiment < 0.3.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment volatility > 0.5 in last 5 days, model tends to lag — add 1–3% upward bias to catch momentum.
- If news volume > 2.0 in last 3 days and sentiment is bullish, model often overestimates — reduce forecast by 3–6%.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days if sentiment is weak.
- Overshoot correction: if model forecast > true outcome by > 2% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–5% unless sentiment is strong.
